title: Align CronDelete tool with the TS baseline
objective: Implement all CronDelete improvements identified by the per-tool subagent report so the Go clone matches the original TypeScript tool in public contract, runtime logic, robustness, state lifecycle, and tests.

context.problem: CronDelete is close at the basic delete-by-id path, but it is not fully aligned with the TS implementation. The main gaps are the Go tool's text-only success contract, collapsed not-found/storage-error handling, missing teammate ownership guard, incomplete runtime kill-switch behavior, and non-strict input parsing.

parallelization_notes: Can be assigned to an implementation subagent after listed dependencies are available. Avoid running concurrently with another task that owns the same files.

improvement_points.title: Success output is text-only and does not preserve the TS structured {id} result contract
improvement_points.description: The TS tool has a typed DeleteOutput with id and then derives both model-facing and UI-facing messages from that output. The Go port only emits a human string, so downstream callers cannot reliably distinguish the stable result value from prose.

improvement_points.title: Delete validation lacks TS-style existence error codes and teammate ownership protection
improvement_points.description: TS separates validation from mutation and protects session-only teammate crons so a teammate can delete only its own jobs. Go has no owner metadata on CronJob and no current-agent check in CronDelete, so any caller that knows an id can delete it.

improvement_points.title: Durable delete storage failures are collapsed into not-found results
improvement_points.description: The Go store returns a bool from delete, so it cannot tell the tool whether the id was absent or durable storage failed. TS preserves that distinction: missing ids are validation errors, while write failures remain operational failures.

improvement_points.title: CronDelete does not enforce the TS runtime cron kill switch at execute time
improvement_points.description: Go has a local kill-switch helper and uses it for CronCreate, but CronDelete ignores it. TS hides CronDelete when the cron feature is disabled, so Go's already-registered delete tool can remain callable after the local disable flag is set.

improvement_points.title: CronDelete input is not strict like the TS z.strictObject schema
improvement_points.description: TS rejects extra fields at schema validation time. Go publishes a schema that cannot express additionalProperties=false and then ignores unknown keys while parsing.

improvement_points.title: CronDelete-specific tests do not lock parity for output, ownership, feature flag, or storage-error behavior
improvement_points.description: Current Go tests prove that a basic session job can be deleted and then disappears from list output. They do not protect the TS-specific contracts that are currently missing.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align CronDelete success output with TS structured id contract
implementation_steps: Change CronDelete success rendering from "Cron job deleted: id=<id>" to the TS-compatible cancellation text.
Expose the deleted id in a stable machine-readable place supported by the Go result layer, such as Metadata["id"], while keeping text output backward-readable.
Add a focused test that asserts success text and id metadata for a created-then-deleted job.
acceptance_criteria: CronDelete success result includes the exact deleted id in a stable field, not only embedded prose.
CronDelete model-facing content matches the TS wording pattern "Cancelled job <id>."
Existing basic delete/list behavior remains unchanged.
risks: Changing visible text can affect tests or callers that parse the old "Cron job deleted: id=" wording.
non_goals: Do not change CronCreate or CronList output contracts in this task.

implementation_subtasks.title: Preserve durable delete errors instead of reporting them as not found
implementation_steps: Change CronStore.delete from bool to a result that carries found/deleted and error separately.
Return a tool-level not-found error only when the id is absent.
Return an infrastructure error or explicit storage ToolResult error when durable read/write fails, following the repo's Tool.Execute error conventions.
Add a test that injects an unreadable/unwritable cron file path or write failure and asserts the result is not a not-found error.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown ids still produce a not-found tool error.
Durable file read/write failures are distinguishable from not-found.
Session-only deletes still remove in-memory schedules.
risks: Filesystem permission tests can be platform-sensitive, especially on Windows or when running as a privileged user.
non_goals: Do not redesign cron file locking or scheduler leadership.

implementation_subtasks.title: Add teammate owner metadata and enforce CronDelete ownership checks
implementation_steps: Identify or add the Go runtime hook that exposes the current in-process agent id to CronCreate/CronDelete.
Store owner/AgentID only on session cron jobs; do not persist it to durable cron JSON.
Reject durable teammate cron creation using the existing guard and attach owner metadata to non-durable teammate cron creation.
Make CronDelete validate ownership before deletion and return an owner-denied tool error distinct from not-found.
Add tests for owner can delete, another owner cannot delete, and leader behavior on unowned jobs.
acceptance_criteria: Session-only teammate jobs carry owner identity in memory.
CronDelete refuses deletion when current agent id differs from the job owner.
Unowned leader-created jobs remain deletable from the leader path.
Durable cron file format remains compatible with TS scheduled_tasks.json.
risks: Go may not yet have an exact AsyncLocalStorage equivalent for in-process teammate identity; this task may need a small runtime context provider.
Owner enforcement must not accidentally block top-level user cleanup of unowned jobs.
non_goals: Do not add owner fields to durable scheduled_tasks.json.
Do not change team mailbox or broader agent lifecycle behavior.

implementation_subtasks.title: Apply cron feature kill-switch behavior to CronDelete
implementation_steps: Add the cronDisabledByFeatureFlag check to CronDelete.Execute before parsing/mutating input.
Return the same refusal style as CronCreate uses through cronFeatureFlagRefusal.
Add a CronDelete-specific feature-flag test with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON=1.
acceptance_criteria: CronDelete refuses execution when CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON is truthy.
CronDelete still works when the disable flag is unset and AGENT_TRIGGERS registered it.
Create/List/Delete feature-flag behavior is internally consistent in Go.
risks: TS hides the tool through isEnabled while Go will return a refusal from an already-registered tool; exact transport parity may require broader registry support later.
non_goals: Do not implement GrowthBook-backed tengu_kairos_cron in this task.

implementation_subtasks.title: Make CronDelete input strict for unknown fields
implementation_steps: Add schema support for additionalProperties=false or add a CronDelete-local unknown-key validator.
Ensure CronDelete rejects inputs with keys other than id.
Add tests for unknown fields and wrong id type.
acceptance_criteria: CronDelete schema or execution path rejects extra keys.
Valid {"id":"..."} input remains accepted.
The implementation does not unintentionally change other tool schemas unless explicitly covered by tests.
risks: Adding additionalProperties to the shared JSONSchema type can affect all tool definitions and snapshots.
A local validator is safer but leaves the advertised API schema less exact.
non_goals: Do not make every Go tool strict in this task.

implementation_subtasks.title: Expand CronDelete parity regression tests
implementation_steps: Add or update tests alongside each behavioral fix rather than creating one broad brittle fixture.
Cover success output/id metadata, unknown id, empty id, unknown fields, feature-disabled refusal, storage failure, and owner-denied deletion.
Keep durable and session-only cases separate so failures identify the affected store.
acceptance_criteria: Each CronDelete gap has a failing-before/passing-after regression test.
Tests assert observable behavior, not private implementation details except where package-private store helpers are already used by cron tests.
Existing cron create/list scheduler tests continue passing.
risks: Some tests depend on changes from other tasks; keep dependency markers clear if landing incrementally.
non_goals: Do not broaden this to all CronCreate/CronList parity tests beyond what CronDelete needs.
